source_text: Per hoc igitur suppetit homini habere proprium bonum, per quod ei subest posse facere malum. Tota ergo divini plenitudo iudicii tam iunctum habet negotium cum hac libertate hominum, ut harum qui unam agnoverit, ambas noverit. Unde fit ut harum unam qui violaverit, ambas violet. Sic igitur et libertas humani custodiatur arbitrii, quemadmodum divina aequitas custoditur. Hic intellectus liberi arbitrii est, qui et fatorum opinionem, et Chaldaeorum supputationem, et Manichaeorum phantasias, veritati ecclesiasticae subiugavit. Hic intellectus est, qui cum illis, quos enumeravimus, vos etiam a Christo monstrat alienos. Libertas igitur arbitrii, possibilitas est vel admittendi, vel vitandi peccati, expers cogentis necessitatis, quae in suo utpote iure habet, utrum surgentium partem sequatur, id est, vel ardua asperaque virtutum, vel demersa et palustria voluptatum.
pass_a_gloss: Through this therefore it is available to a human to have a proper good, through which it underlies him to be able to do evil. The whole fullness therefore of divine judgment has so joined a business with this liberty of humans, that of these whoever shall have recognized one, has known both. Whence it happens that of these whoever shall have violated one, violates both. So therefore let also the liberty of human choice be guarded, just as divine equity is guarded. This understanding of free choice is that which subjected both the opinion of fates, and the computation of the Chaldeans, and the fantasies of the Manichaeans, to ecclesiastical truth. This understanding is that which with those whom we have enumerated shows you also alien from Christ. The liberty of choice therefore is a possibility either of admitting or of avoiding sin, without a compelling necessity, which has in its own right as it were, whether it follow the part of things rising, that is, either the steep and rough of virtues, or the sunken and marshy of pleasures.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS libertas; Blaise moral freedom to will or refuse
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice

pass_b_english: A person can therefore possess a good that is his own precisely because he also has the capacity to do evil. The entire fullness of divine judgment is so closely bound up with this human freedom that whoever recognizes one knows both. Consequently, whoever violates one violates both. Let the freedom of human choice therefore be preserved just as divine fairness is preserved. This is the understanding of free choice that has subjected belief in fate, the calculations of Chaldean astrologers, and the fantasies of the Manichaeans to the Church's truth. This is the understanding that shows you too, along with those we have listed, to be strangers to Christ. Freedom of choice, then, is the capacity either to commit or to avoid sin, free from compelling necessity. It has within its own authority which of the alternatives that arise it follows: either the steep and rugged heights of the virtues or the sunken marshes of pleasures.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
